about: The carrier's design, from the ship designer (design/ship-designer.html: Copy JSON). Sections run bow to stern; SHIP-DESIGN.md says what it means. This is the design, not the game's layout: ships/carrier/ is what the game plays.
name: Twin-drum carrier
notes:
The chosen carrier. Bow with torpedoes and point defence, an armoured sleeve round the spin drum, a long vacuum hangar with six turrets and sixteen broadside tubes, and a short stern with the bridge tower.

The drum is now two halves inside the one sleeve, spinning opposite ways. One drum this big would act as a gyroscope the RCS could barely turn. The pair cancels out and looks the same from outside.

Rooms: 40 round each ring, about 10 m wide, so floors lean only 4.5° at the edges. Each half is one 22 m ring: 80 rooms of about 10 × 20 m on two decks, 160 in all. That holds the ~730 aboard with about a third spare for growth, passengers or evacuees. Shortening the drum from 112 m to 44 m took about 180,000 t off the ship.

Getting about: each ring has a 3 m corridor right round it on both decks, with rooms fore and aft, so nobody walks through rooms. Six spokes per ring each carry two lifts and a ladder tube, from a hub ring that turns round the fixed spine corridor. You catch the hub ring at walking pace, ride about 45 s down 55 m, and get heavier the whole way. The spine runs bow to stern through a pressurised tunnel along the top of the airless hangar, with boarding tubes down to the fighters. Most action stations are in the weightless hull, so at general quarters the drum empties up the spokes in about 4 to 5 minutes.

Outside in, the 8 m ring is: a 2 m belt of water tanks and stores, then two 3 m decks of rooms (0.97 g and 0.92 g). A shell has to get through the 0.5 m steel sleeve, a 2.5 m gap and the belt before it reaches anyone. Battleships protected their sides the same way, with alternating empty and liquid-filled layers in front of the main armour. The water also shields the crew from radiation, and pumping it between tanks keeps the drum balanced after damage. Solid steel instead would be stronger, but a 1 m steel belt weighs about 360,000 t. Each room is about the size of today's mess or gym. Lifts run up the spokes to the corridor at 6 points round each ring. Messes, the sick bay and ops sit beside the lifts, with berths in the quieter stretches between. The combat CIC stays in the fixed, armoured hull; the drum has planning and briefing rooms.
